headline: USB PD is the closest thing to a universal fast charging standard
summary: With USB PD 3.1 supporting up to 240W and PPS offering precise power delivery, it's the go-to for most modern devices.
details: The world of fast charging is a confusing jungle of proprietary standards like Qualcomm's Quick Charge, Oppo's SuperVOOC, and Xiaomi's HyperCharge. However, USB Power Delivery (USB PD) is emerging as the closest thing to a universal standard, widely adopted across phones, tablets, and laptops.

Newer versions of USB PD are pushing power limits, with USB PD 3.1 supporting up to 240W, primarily targeting demanding devices like laptops. For smartphones, which don't require such extreme power levels due to thermal constraints, USB PD with its PPS feature is ideal.

PPS, or Programmable Power Supply, is a key feature of USB PD that allows devices to request smaller, more precise voltage and current adjustments. This improves charging efficiency and helps manage heat, crucial for extending battery lifespan.

Samsung's Galaxy S26 Ultra utilizes PPS for its 60W "Super Fast Charging 3.0," while Google's Pixel 11 models leverage USB-C PPS for their fastest charging speeds, with the Pro model optimized for a 45W PPS charger.

While proprietary systems from OnePlus, Oppo, and Xiaomi can offer very high charging speeds, they often require specific chargers and cables. Many of these devices also support USB-C PD, though speeds may not match their proprietary counterparts.

It's important to note that manufacturer claims of 80W or 100W charging don't mean continuous power draw. Devices typically charge fastest at lower battery percentages and then taper off as they fill up.

Concerns about fast charging degrading battery health are largely mitigated by modern device management. Phones can monitor temperature, reduce power when necessary, and taper charging as the battery approaches full, ensuring long-term battery health.
While fast charging is generally safe, if you're not in a hurry, a slower, standard charge can still be beneficial for maximizing battery longevity over many years.

headline_marked: [[Smart Scraper M2M]] API Slashes AI Agent Scraping Time to ~30ms
headline: Smart Scraper M2M API Slashes AI Agent Scraping Time to ~30ms
summary: A new machine-to-machine scraper API promises to significantly speed up web scraping for AI agents, reducing latency and token costs.
details: Building AI agents with frameworks like CrewAI or LangChain can be hindered by slow and resource-intensive web scraping. This process often bloats context windows and increases the token costs associated with Large Language Models (LLMs).

To address this challenge, a developer has created Smart Scraper M2M, a lightweight and high-performance web scraper API. It is specifically engineered for machine-to-machine (M2M) communication, aiming to streamline data acquisition for AI systems.

The API boasts an impressive scraping time of approximately 30 milliseconds, a significant improvement over traditional methods. This speed is crucial for real-time AI applications that require rapid data processing.

The developer has made the full source code available on GitHub, encouraging community contributions and feedback. This open-source approach allows for transparency and collaborative improvement of the tool.

Users can test the API directly and explore its capabilities. The developer is actively seeking thoughts, feature requests, and contributions to further enhance the scraper's performance and functionality.
